title: Thanks AI, I hate it. I was always a horror fan, so I made my version of Henry James' The Turn of the Screw. I had to skip nights developing in because I was too scared.
author: igotlagg
selftext:
I'm a huge horror fan, movies and games alike, and I've always wanted to make my own story-driven horror game with some first-person action. So I'm building one around Henry James' *The Turn of the Screw*, set at Bly.

It's 1970. You are the new governess at Bly, a country house in Essex, hired to look after 8-year-old Flora and her brother Miles. The children are lovely. The house has rules: don't speak of her, don't look for her, and when the clock strikes three, be somewhere she won't look.

The "fun" part of AI development is that I don't know exactly how everything works under the hood, so I get to experience my own game from an unknown perspective. I can only work on it after dark, and the scary scenes have me on the edge of my seat, lol.

Everything in the trailer is in-game footage. Happy to answer questions about the workflow.

Anyone else here love this genre?

comments.author: Lambisexual
comments.body: What did you do for the characters? Especially to get them facial rigs

replies.author: igotlagg
replies.body: I used mouth sprite sheets and asked AI to link it to the sound and tones, so it’s dynamic. Was a bit of tweekinh but works wonderfully. Too bas it looks too low poly, maybe I should try to find some more realistic models

replies.author: Lambisexual
replies.body: Interesting. But the models themselves are just bought assets?

replies.author: igotlagg
replies.body: Yes, with a little bit of tweaking here and there. Its synty assets

replies.author: Lambisexual
replies.body: Ahh Synty, no wonder I recognized it.

replies.author: igotlagg
replies.body: The goat for prototyping. And I’d imagine, if I can make synty assets scary, the atmosphere is good.
